title: Unique extension of labelled stable isomorphisms over an arbitrary trait
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $n\ge0$, and let $(W,s_1,\ldots,s_n)$ and $(W',s'_1,\ldots,s'_n)$ be stable pointed curves over $S$ [def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve]. Fix a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Let $R$ be any discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction field $K$, and let $b:\operatorname{Spec}R\to S$ be any morphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Use fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] to form $W_R,W'_R,W_K,W'_K$ and all pulled-back sections. Every $K$-isomorphism $u_K:W_K\xrightarrow{\sim}W'_K$ satisfying $u_K\circ s_{i,K}=s'_{\sigma(i),K}$ for all $i$ is the restriction of exactly one $R$-isomorphism $u_R:W_R\xrightarrow{\sim}W'_R$ satisfying $u_R\circ s_{i,R}=s'_{\sigma(i),R}$ for all $i$. The DVR need not be excellent or of finite type over $S$; its generic point need not map to a generic point of $S$. No smoothness of $W_K$ or $W'_K$ and no identity condition on $u_K$ are assumed. Marking equalities are equalities of section morphisms.

source.place: Agent marked and persistently nodal extension of the log-canonical common-model route motivated by Tag 0E97 (lemma-unique-stable-model). proof.text: Put $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $X=W_R$, $Y=W'_R$, and relabel the target marks as $t_i=s'_{\sigma(i),R}$. Both pulled-back families are H-projective: apply [lem-trf-projective-bundle-affine-presentations] to each bundle embedding from [def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve]. Choose a resulting open neighbourhood of the image under $b$ of the closed point of $T$. Its inverse image contains that closed point and hence all of $T$ (every prime of the local ring $R$ is contained in its maximal ideal). Thus $b$ factors through this neighbourhood. Compose the two closed embeddings there; the composite is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-products], and pull back using [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Projective space pulls back to projective space by its fibre-product definition [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. This gives a finite-projective-space embedding over $T$ for each family. Flatness and finite presentation follow from [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). Every geometric fibre with its marked sections is the original geometric fibre for the composite geometric point into $S$, by associativity of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. Consequently all nodal, reducedness, connectedness, dimension, smooth-marking and component-stability conditions in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve] hold over $T$. The relative smooth locus $W^{\mathrm{sm}}\subset W$ is open and smooth over $S$; it is the disjoint union of the opens on which its relative dimension is a fixed $n$ (locally constant by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]). By [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](1) each of their pullbacks to $T$, an open subscheme of $W_R$, is smooth over $T$, hence lies in the relative smooth locus of $W_R\to T$ and contains the pulled sections; likewise for $W'$. The relabelled $u_K$ preserves every label.

proof.text: A DVR is Noetherian by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], so $T$ is locally Noetherian. Apply [lem-sfb-nodal-log-canonical-reconstruction] to $X/T$ and $Y/T$. Write $D_X=\sum_i s_i(T)$, $D_Y=\sum_i t_i(T)$ and $L_X=\omega_{X/T}(D_X)$, $L_Y=\omega_{Y/T}(D_Y)$. For each normalized geometric component $C$, its stated degree formula is $2g(C)-2+r_C$. This is positive: for $g=0$, stability gives $r_C\ge3$; for $g=1$, it gives $r_C\ge1$; for $g\ge2$, it is at least $2$. Thus both log-dualizing modules are relatively ample, and the same node gives canonical isomorphisms $r_X:X\simeq\operatorname{Proj}A_X$ and $r_Y:Y\simeq\operatorname{Proj}A_Y$, where $A_X=\bigoplus_{m\ge0}H^0(X,L_X^{\otimes m})$ and likewise for $Y$. This includes degree zero and an empty marking.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-semistable-log-pluricanonical-lattices] to $X,Y$ and $u_K$, with the labels just fixed. Its hypotheses are exactly the projective flat finitely presented nodal families with disjoint smooth marks of step 1; it imposes neither excellence nor smoothness of the generic fibre. Generic restriction is injective in every degree, and $u_K^*$ identifies the image of $H^0(Y,L_Y^{\otimes m})$ with that of $H^0(X,L_X^{\otimes m})$. Thus each section on $Y$ has a unique section on $X$ with generic restriction its canonical pullback. The multiplication and unit compatibility in the cited statement makes these bijections a graded unital $R$-algebra isomorphism $\Phi:A_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X$.

proof.text: By [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality](2), $\Phi$ gives the contravariant isomorphism $P:\operatorname{Proj}A_X\simeq\operatorname{Proj}A_Y$. Define $u_R=r_Y^{-1}P r_X$. Check its generic restriction as follows. Both families are proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The field $K$ is the localization $R[1/\pi]$, so is flat over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]. Apply [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] with $i=0$ to each $L^{\otimes m}$: its canonical map identifies $A_X\otimes_R K$ and $A_Y\otimes_R K$ with the full generic section algebras. These identifications preserve multiplication, since $(s/\pi^a)(t/\pi^b)=st/\pi^{a+b}$. Step 3 then says that $\Phi\otimes_R K$ is precisely the canonical graded pullback by $u_K$. The flat Proj base change of [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality](4) identifies $P_K$ with its Proj map. The reconstruction maps restrict to the generic reconstruction maps: on a standard chart their formulas are $t/s^a\mapsto t/s^a$, as stated in [lem-sfb-proper-ample-section-proj-reconstruction], and localization at $\pi$ preserves these formulas. Its isomorphism-naturality gives $P_K r_{X_K}=r_{Y_K}u_K$. Substituting in the definition proves $(u_R)_K=u_K$.

proof.text: We verify the hypotheses for a separated-target uniqueness argument. The target $Y/T$ is proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], hence separated. The source $X$ is reduced and $X_K\to X$ has dense image: in every local ring of the flat $R$-scheme $X$, multiplication by $\pi$ is injective (tensor the injection $R\xrightarrow{\pi}R$ with a flat module). Thus the structure sheaf injects into its localization at $\pi$. That localization is the reduced generic fibre; reducedness follows from the given geometric reducedness, since tensoring a vector space with a field extension is injective (extend a nonzero vector to a basis), and a nilpotent remains nilpotent after extension. A nilpotent local section is therefore zero, so $X$ is reduced. Every nonempty affine open meets $D(\pi)$: otherwise $\pi$ would be nilpotent in its ring, contradicting injectivity of multiplication by $\pi$. Hence $X_K$ is dense. Also $T$ is reduced and $\operatorname{Spec}K\to T$ is dense because $R$ is a domain. These are elementary consequences of flatness and the DVR hypotheses [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring].

proof.text: For each $i$, the two $T$-morphisms $u_R s_i,t_i:T\to Y$ agree after $\operatorname{Spec}K\to T$ by step 4 and the prescribed generic marking equations. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext], using reducedness of $T$, density of its generic point and separatedness of $Y/T$ from step 5. It gives $u_R s_i=t_i$ as section morphisms. If $v_R$ is any other $R$-isomorphism with generic restriction $u_K$, apply that same lemma to $u_R,v_R:X\to Y$ and the dense map $X_K\to X$; step 5 verifies reducedness of $X$ and separatedness of the target. Thus $v_R=u_R$. Relabelling back proves the required permutation equations and uniqueness. No step used the image of the generic point of $T$ being generic in $S$.
